Sure, here are two hints for each step of the problem:

**Step: Milad has performed one-hot encoding on one column.**

*Hint 1:* One-hot encoding is a process of converting categorical variables into a form that could be provided to ML algorithms to do a better job in prediction. In this case, each unique genre becomes a separate column with binary values indicating the presence of that genre.

*Hint 2:* When using one-hot encoding, one of the categories is typically dropped to avoid multicollinearity. This is because the presence of all categories can be perfectly predicted by the others, which can cause issues in linear regression models.
